slides.title: GALEN COLLEGE OF NURSINGLIVE REVIEW
text: System Focused Review-OB and Newborn Care

slides.title: Signs and Symptoms of Pregnancy
text: Perceived by the examiner & only caused by pregnancy

slides.title: Reproductive System Adaptations
text: Uterus moves out of pelvis into abdomen after 3 months
Fundal height by 20 weeks gestation at level of umbilicus
Reliable determination of gestational age until 36 weeks gestation

slides.title: Reproductive System Adaptations
text: Increased vascularization and violet color (Chadwick's sign)
Thickening and lengthening of vaginal vault
Secretions more acidic, white, and thick (leukorrhea)
Increase in size to prepare for lactation
Nipples become pronounced, erect and darker color

slides.title: Integumentary System Adaptations
text: Increase in hair and nail growth

slides.title: Musculoskeletal System Adaptations
text: Softening and stretching of ligaments holding sacroiliac joints and pubis symphysis-“waddling gait”
Forward shifting of center of gravity

slides.title: Antepartum(Prenatal)
text: Focus on education for overall wellness
Detection and prevention of potential problems
Comprehensive health history, physical examination, and laboratory tests
Calculation of estimated or expected date of birth (EDB) or delivery (EDD)

slides.title: Obstetric History
text: Primipara: one birth after a pregnancy of at least 20 weeks
Multipara: two or more pregnancies resulting in viable offspring
Abortions: birth that occurs <20 weeks gestation

slides.title: Obstetric History
text: What if the client is pregnant with twins?

slides.title: Physical Examination
text: Crown to rump measurement accurate up through 12 weeks

slides.title: Follow-up Visits
text: Triple or Quad screen- neural tube defect at 16-18 wks.
UA, also for protein and glucose (each visit)

slides.title: Fetal Kick Counts
text: Note amount of time to count 10 movements
Notify physician if:  <10 kicks in two consecutive hours
Count movements for 1 hour after a meal, should feel > 4
If < 4 movements felt, continue to monitor movements for a second hour
Notify physician if < 4 movements felt in an hour

slides.title: Magnesium Sulfate
text: Indicated in pregnancy: preeclampsia, preterm labor
Action:  blocks neuromuscular transmission; relaxes smooth muscle,
decreases BP, slows/ decreases intensity of uterine contractions
Considerations: monitor for therapeutic Mg Sulfate levels
Monitor: Resp. rate, urine output, DTRs, FHR, BP, contractions
SE: flushing, “warmth”, nasal congestion, N/V, constipation, HA, blurred vision.
What are magnesium sulfate therapeutic levels and what is the antidote?

slides.title: TORCH
text: Parasite contracted through cat feces; under-cooked meats
Teratogenic in first trimester, causes congenital defects of the fetus
Virus causing low birthweight, blindness, enlarged spleen/liver
Culture if active lesions; treat with acyclovir, can cause death of newborn

slides.title: Regular contractions
text: Contractions start in back radiate to abdomen
Walking has no effect, or lessens contractions
Contractions do not decrease with rest or warm bath
Rest and warm bath lessen contractions

slides.title: 4.  Psychological Response
text: Childbirth is life-altering experience influenced greatly by the female's psyche/ state of mind.

slides.title: Phases of Labor
text: First stage: onset of labor to complete cervical dilation
Second stage: complete dilation to delivery of baby
Third stage: birth to delivery of placenta
Fourth stage: 1-4 hours after placenta delivered

slides.title: Stage
text: Request medications, C/S to “get it over with”

slides.title: Latent phase (0-3cm)
text: Pack bags/ last minute preparations before hospitalization

slides.title: Active Phase (4-7cm)
text: Most providers advise going to hospital when contractions occur every  3-5 mins., lasting 45-60 secs. OR if membranes rupture

slides.title: Transition Phase (8-10cm)
text: Frequency  every 2- 3 mins., duration lasts 45-90 secs.
Assess maternal VS at least every 30mins.
Ice, lubricant for lips/ dry mouth

slides.title: Back Labor (POP)
text: Assess fetal position w/ Leopold maneuver

slides.title: Cardinal Movements

slides.title: Malposition
text: External (or cephalic) version of the fetus.
A new technique involves pressure on the fetal head and buttocks so that the fetus completes a “backward flip” or “forward roll.”
